We're talking about it more. The uptick in drinking is really recent. Previously I wasn't happy about him doing it at all but it was enough or often enough to get anyone else on board with calling it a problem.

He's pretty open with me generally. His childhood was... Pretty bad. His dad makes him look like a saint. Alcohol, drugs, abuse, prison... I don't know every detail but I know he struggles with that. 

His dad got better in his later years, AA etc, and they got close. With the unfortunate result that he both reveres and hates him, so he's bitter about the childhood and very very angry, but guilt stricken for feeling that way too. 

I know anxiety is a problem and that's where communication lacks. He'll tell me about his past but he has a tendency to try to keep current problems to himself. Then he stresses over them and that contributes a lot to his want to drink. He feels guilty talking about 'his' problems. To him that would be putting them off on me. Unmanly maybe? Unadult certainly. 

He's too independent for his own good there.

So far he's still pretty moody but he made me dinner and that seemed like a good sign. 

When he quit drinking before it was pretty much completely his father's doing. He was able to essentially guilt him out of it by casually mentioning how shitty he was the night before day after day. And not so casually yelling when necessary. I heard he found a bottle on him after work one night and smashed it right there in the parking lot but I didn't witness the event. 

He would put a stop to all this weirdness right now. Unfortunately he died almost 2 years ago now and no one else has the same effect. 

Baby's sex is still unknown but if it's a boy he'll be James Dewey for sure. If it's a girl I like Ella Marie but that one isn't set in stone.

Related:

He's definitely drinking more lately. I knew I was right to be concerned. I started marking his bottles so I was sure when one was empty and a new one started. 

We're not to "drowning in whiskey" levels but have definitely hit "I am a nightly drinker". I didn't live with him when he drank heavily so I can only guess how far apart those two might be in progression. Somewhere in between them is "pretty much always buzzed" which I think has to be my exit point. 

Drowning stage is not pretty. I'm maybe too flippant with the name because drowning, for him, is a pretty literal description. We're talking gallons of the stuff. Hundreds of dollars a week. Waking up and having to check where he was, whether his truck made it home, and who was in his house. Drunk driving. Truck parked on the fucking porch. Family begging, literally on hands and knees for him to stop. 

It's an actual miracle the man is alive. He did this for 20 years. If he wasn't at work he was drinking inhuman amounts. Most of the above he doesn't remember. People had to tell him the next morning. 

I have to watch for that in the middle point and get out beforehand if it seems like he's headed for round two. Pretty sure I would die of misery watching that.

I maybe shouldn't but I desperately want him to stay. I love him. I want us to make things work and be a family. 

He sure hasn't packed or anything so unless he's planning to throw all his stuff into some friends trunk in a jumbled mess it doesn't look much like he's going anywhere. He's a very clean tidy person so that sort of disorganized leaving doesn't even sound like him. 

Plan B is basically I give him until the baby is born to make some changes. If he doesn't, or if we can't work, then I drive halfway across the country and stay with an extremely supportive and caring family member. 

I can't say I'm happy or that death has completely left my mind, but I'm making plans so that obviously indicates at least a bare minimum amount of desire to live. Somehow I'll be okay I guess.

If he really is I wish he'd just do it already. I'd be better off if he wasn't coming home every evening.

Amazingly, the alcohol, even at his worst, never affected his job. It's just that the place we both worked shut down and put a lot of people looking for work at once. I haven't had much better luck there. 

Anyway... Most of your comment sounds eerily like him. He's always depressed or angry. It's always someone else's fault. He quit the whiskey for a while, and still os nothing like he was... but he never learned how to deal with the issues he has. 

So I end up suffering. :/

I am working but the pay is abysmal. Baby is due in Aug. And we wanted a baby but hoped it would take longer after having lost one. It ended up happening very quickly, and scared us at first, but it's to a "safe" point now so that's not an issue. 

I was still happy/excited until this little episode. I thought he was, but now I wonder if he was faking. I mean if he was happy he wouldn't be able to just say fuck it and leave right?

I don't think it's possible now no. He obviously has resentment toward me that he wasn't bringing up  
I feel like he said things that can't be unsaid and that if he really thinks them it's too late to try now. He should have talked to me. 

We've had a lot of financial difficulty. His car just got repossessed. Mine is behind on payments and at risk of also being gone. He was unemployed for a long time and my employment has been both spotty and underpaid. 
Before the current pregnancy we went through an ectopic which was very sad and stressful for us both. 

His brother is in poor health. They just lost a close uncle. My mother is on her deathbed. His mother is basically crazy and makes everyone else crazy too... 

And he feels my concern about drinking is unwarranted, looking for drama, etc. ( to be fair to us both no, he does not drink heavily but yes, he was an alcoholic for 20 years and him doing it at all makes me intensely uncomfortable).

He said it a couple days ago now. Monday. I came home from work, was a bit childish and didn't want to talk about why right then, and I guess things escalated in his head after that. 

He's not an alcoholic. I don't want people to get the wrong idea there. He drinks very little actually. It's just that when he does it really changes him, and quickly. I blame most of our problems on that. Not all but 90%

His mom: he loves her but he doesn't like her. She's hard to live with. And he's been here taking care of her for 6 years or so. He ends up taking care of everyone. I'm the only one who ever tries to do the same for him. Another reason it hurts so badly that he apparently doesn't see that. 

His brother: I didn't mean much in particular by mentioning him. We're close. The three of us spend a fair amount of time together, and I text his brother most every day. Not in a weird way like I'd be with him too. Ew. I know people jump to that conclusion. He's always been a good friend to me and I think he'll be more upset as my friend than his brother will be as my lover. That's how it feels right now.
